content: Data tracking the MHSA Compliance Rate within the mining communications market from 2020 to 2024 illustrates an overall increasing trend. The compliance rate climbed steadily from a minimum of 70.0 percent in 2020 to an impressive maximum of 98.0 percent in 2024. This high rate of compliance indicates that communication service providers and mining operators have successfully integrated MHSA standards into their technological deployment strategies, ensuring that the rapid adoption of new communication tools does not compromise the occupational health and safety mandates enforced by the state. The broader regulatory environment in South Africa is also undergoing significant transformation, which may indirectly influence MHSA compliance frameworks for telecommunications. Recent regulatory developments, including proposed amendments to the Radio Frequency Spectrum Amendment Regulations as of May 2026, highlight evolving compliance requirements for satellite internet services, though they do not reference MHSA compliance explicitly [36] . Furthermore, discussions surrounding a potential Digital Economy Act suggest that South Africa is actively working towards modernizing and consolidating its digital and telecommunications industry regulations [53] . Such a unified regulatory framework could potentially include new implications for MHSA compliance as part of broader occupational safety mandates [53] . Additionally, references to regulations published in April 2026 and their drafting processes mention no explicit ties to MHSA, leaving gaps in relevant specifics [54] . Some sources are outdated for contemporary analysis, as regulations and market dynamics may have evolved significantly since publication, particularly for cybersecurity developments reported in January 2023 [51] . The ongoing focus on health and safety standards at an operational level was recently underscored by an MHSA conference held in Johannesburg from June 30 to July 1, 2026, which featured prominent industry figures discussing operational safety [28] . While it remains unclear whether direct links to telecommunications were discussed at this event, the continuous dialogue around MHSA emphasizes its critical role in all mining-related activities [28] .
